Posterior probability of a safety signal under the BDRIBS model

Source: R/bdribs_post.R
bdribs_post.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of the relative risk under the Poisson-based BDRIBS model of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) as specified in Duncan (2026). With the total exposure time as exposure, the model is BDRIBS(1); with the total time at risk (time after the first occurrence of the event removed), it is BDRIBS(2). Both can be computed from subject-level data with time_at_risk.

Usage

bdribs_post(
  y,
  exposure,
  k = 1,
  lambda_hp,
  pt_hp,
  df = 1,
  p_prior = c(0.5, 0.5),
  rr0 = 1,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  t_star = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  details = TRUE
)

Arguments

y

Number of subjects with the event in the blinded data (non-negative integer).

exposure

Total exposure time (BDRIBS(1)) or total time at risk (BDRIBS(2)) of the blinded population (positive).

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to placebo (k:1).

lambda_hp

Event rate in the historical placebo population.

pt_hp

Total patient time at risk in the historical placebo population, or Inf for a known background rate lambda_hp.

df

Discount factor for the historical data (df >= 1 discounts the historical information).

p_prior

Shape parameters c(a, b) of the Beta prior for \(p\). The default c(0.5, 0.5) is the prior used by Duncan (2026).

rr0

Critical value of the rate ratio (\(\theta_c\) in Duncan, 2026).

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

t_star

Optional time at which the cumulative incidences are summarized.

level

Probability of the equal-tailed credible interval of the rate ratio.

details

Logical; if FALSE, only prob, signal and incidence are computed, and rr and estimates are NA. This is faster and is used in sim_oc.

Value

An object of class bssd_post, a list with elements

model

"BDRIBS".

prob

Posterior probability \(P(r > rr_0 \mid Y)\).

signal

Logical; prob > cutoff.

rr

Posterior mean, median, and the limits of the equal-tailed credible interval of \(r\).

estimates

Posterior means of \(p\), \(r\), the placebo event rate \(\delta\) (lambda_p) and the study drug event rate \(r \delta\) (lambda_d).

incidence

Posterior means of the cumulative incidences at t_star for placebo and study drug and of their difference, or NULL when t_star is not given.

rr_label, rr0, cutoff, level, t_star

Settings used.

data, prior

Data summary and prior parameters.

integration

Description of the numerical integration.

Details

The model is $$Y \sim \mathrm{Poisson}[E \delta (r k + 1) / (k + 1)],$$ $$\delta \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\lambda_{HP} PT_{HP} / DF, PT_{HP} / DF),$$ $$r = p / [k (1 - p)], \quad p \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a, b),$$ where \(Y\) is the number of subjects with the event, \(E\) is the exposure, \(k\) is the randomization ratio (study drug to placebo \(k:1\)), \(\delta\) is the event rate in the placebo group, and \(r\) is the rate ratio of study drug to placebo. The Gamma distribution is parameterized by shape and rate.

Because the Gamma prior is conjugate to the Poisson likelihood, \(\delta\) is integrated out analytically, and the marginal posterior density of \(p\) is proportional to $$p^{a - 1} (1 - p)^{b + \alpha - 1} [E + \beta (k + 1) (1 - p)]^{-(\alpha + Y)}$$ with \(\alpha = \lambda_{HP} PT_{HP} / DF\) and \(\beta = PT_{HP} / DF\). All posterior quantities are one-dimensional integrals over \(\mathrm{logit}(p)\), which are evaluated by adaptive quadrature (integrate) with a relative tolerance of 1e-10.

A signal is declared when \(P(r > rr_0 \mid Y) > \) cutoff (Duncan, 2026, Equation 3).

When t_star is given, the posterior means of the cumulative incidences at t_star are computed under the exponential distribution implied by the constant event rates, that is, \(1 - \exp(-\delta t^*)\) for placebo and \(1 - \exp(-r \delta t^*)\) for study drug.

With pt_hp = Inf, the prior of \(\delta\) is a point mass at lambda_hp, so the inference is conditional on a known background rate. This is the screening analysis of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) and corresponds to inf.type = 1 of the bdribs package; the marginal posterior density of \(p\) is then proportional to $$p^{a - 1} (1 - p)^{b - Y - 1} \exp[-E \lambda_{HP} / ((k + 1) (1 - p))].$$

The time unit of exposure, lambda_hp, pt_hp and t_star must be the same.

References

Duncan, B. (2026). Robust safety monitoring and signal detection using alternatives to the standard Poisson distribution. Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics, 36(2), 227–244. doi:10.1080/10543406.2024.2395532

Mukhopadhyay, S., Waterhouse, B., and Hartford, A. (2018). Bayesian detection of potential risk using inference on blinded safety data. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 17(6), 823–834. doi:10.1002/pst.1898

See also

time_at_risk, expbern_post, llbern_post

Examples

# 5 subjects with the event in 500 patient-years, randomization 2:1,
# historical placebo rate 18 / 4000 per patient-year
fit <- bdribs_post(y = 5, exposure = 500, k = 2, lambda_hp = 18 / 4000,
                   pt_hp = 4000)
fit
#> Model: BDRIBS 
#> Relative risk: rate ratio r of study drug to placebo
#> P(r > 1 | data) = 0.8199
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of r: mean 2.451, median 2.123, 95% interval (0.195, 6.588)

# known background rate of 0.011 per patient-year and uniform prior for p
# (hypothetical example 2 of Mukhopadhyay et al., 2018)
bdribs_post(y = 9, exposure = 540, k = 2, lambda_hp = 0.011, pt_hp = Inf,
            p_prior = c(1, 1))
#> Model: BDRIBS 
#> Relative risk: rate ratio r of study drug to placebo
#> P(r > 1 | data) = 0.753
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of r: mean 1.522, median 1.438, 95% interval (0.379, 3.143)
